How we work

Editorial Policy

The standards every IMMA News story, guide and update is held to.

Last updated: 25 November 2026

Who we are and who we serve

IMMA News is a Kenyan digital publication based in Nairobi and owned by IMMA Media. We cover Kenyan current affairs, Nairobi, politics, sport, public health, food and nutrition, and the public services Kenyans use every day, and we explain international news that matters to Kenyan readers.

Accuracy

  • We publish only what we can verify. If the central claim of a story cannot be confirmed, we do not publish the story. How we check is set out in our Fact-Checking Policy.
  • Claims we cannot confirm independently are attributed to the person or organisation making them, and we say when something has not been confirmed (for example, an alleged data breach that the government is still investigating).
  • Headlines, summaries and photo captions must match the story. We do not use misleading or sensational headlines to attract clicks.
  • Every story shows the date it was published, and the date of any meaningful update.

Sources and attribution

  • Each story lists the reporting, official statements and documents it is based on, with links where they are available.
  • When we build on reporting by another news organisation, we credit that organisation by name.
  • We prefer primary sources: government notices, court records, official statistics, statements from the organisations involved, and recognised health authorities.
  • We do not rely on anonymous sources for factual claims. If we ever need to protect a source, an editor must know who the source is, and we explain to readers why the source is not named.

Health, nutrition and practical guides

  • Health and nutrition content is general information, not personal medical advice. Guides encourage readers to speak to a qualified health worker about their own situation.
  • Medical and nutrition facts are checked against recognised authorities such as the World Health Organization, Kenya's Ministry of Health and national health services, and these sources are listed on each guide.
  • Estimates, such as the nutrition values of a recipe, are labelled as estimates and explain how they were worked out.
  • Guides to fees, documents and government services link to the official source, which is always the final authority, and are updated when the rules change.

Fairness, independence and conduct

  • We aim to be fair to the people and organisations we write about. Where a story makes a serious allegation, we include the response of those involved when it is available.
  • Editorial decisions are made by the newsroom. Advertisers and sponsors have no say over what we report, and we do not accept payment to publish, change or remove news.
  • We take particular care with children, victims of crime and accidents, and people in grief, and we do not publish details that would identify a child at risk.
  • We do not publish hate speech or content that incites violence.
  • We follow the Code of Conduct for the Practice of Journalism in Kenya, overseen by the Media Council of Kenya.

News, opinion and advertising

  • News reports and guides are kept separate from opinion. Opinion and analysis pieces are labelled as such.
  • Adverts and sponsored content are always labelled and follow our Advertising Terms.

Photos and images

Photos are licensed for reuse and credited. Pictures that illustrate a topic rather than show the actual event are labelled as illustrative, and AI-generated images are labelled as such.

Corrections

When we get something wrong, we correct it promptly and openly. Where a correction changes the meaning of a story, we say so on the story. See Corrections & Complaints to report an error.

Ownership and funding

IMMA News is owned and published by IMMA Media, a Kenyan content, broadcast and production company in Nairobi. It is funded by advertising and sponsorship, which are kept separate from our journalism. See our Masthead for how to reach the newsroom.
